findings: The raw interview caption preserves two files containing hundreds of millions of URLs, a maximum URL length of 64 bytes, and the duplicate-finding goal; it does not require Bloom filters, hash partitioning, a memory budget, URL normalization, or multiplicity semantics.
The candidate explicitly separates normalized method hints from raw-source constraints and labels exact-string unique intersection as a reference contract.
The routing invariant is correct: equal URLs always use the same deterministic partition, while final full-string equality prevents hash or bucket collisions from becoming false matches.
An independently written exhaustive bounded oracle compares the partition strategy with direct set intersection across 7,225 input-pair combinations and a forced same-bucket collision case.
The answer covers oversized/skewed buckets, exactness, optional Bloom prefiltering, duplicate semantics, recovery, parallelism, observability, and does not fabricate production experience.
